<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **16** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 50169dcecd571b63317a584448a9b2d1ba5bf751` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `75a8900a7560356b7586619b6c247578c3e46322` — the merge of head `e71bf1e5764a9e4c0715bb773551ad0cda59dff1` into base `50169dcecd571b63317a584448a9b2d1ba5bf751`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 75a8900a7560356b7586619b6c247578c3e46322 && git checkout 75a8900a7560356b7586619b6c247578c3e46322
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 50169dcecd571b63317a584448a9b2d1ba5bf751 e71bf1e5764a9e4c0715bb773551ad0cda59dff1 && git checkout -B drift-repro 50169dcecd571b63317a584448a9b2d1ba5bf751 && git merge --no-ff e71bf1e5764a9e4c0715bb773551ad0cda59dff1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 50169dcecd571b63317a584448a9b2d1ba5bf751
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 50169dcecd571b63317a584448a9b2d1ba5bf751` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `033fc75a09f8205f05a060cd29b05e449c9afea0`

Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/controlled-by-parent-write-shape-master-edit.test.ts, .changeset/25012-cbp-write-shape-master-edit.md + packages/metadata-core/src/engine-update-dispatch.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/engine-delete-dispatch.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/spec/src/data/bulk-write-hook-conformance.ts, docs/adr/0055-master-detail-controlled-by-parent.md, docs/adr/0139-engine-internal-semi-join-leaf-readable-parent-ids.md

Disclosure: the maintainer's ruling on #9387 (`5323310017`) governs this record; reach is stated abstractly, no probe, grant shape, request body or served value is written here.

### ① Derived judgments

**Governing text and the ruling it must not cross.** ADR-0055 §3 (`docs/adr/0055-master-detail-controlled-by-parent.md:60`): editing, deleting or creating a detail requires edit access to its master, no write shape exempt. Ruling B on #24932 (`6303721609`): the master-scope mechanism moves to the engine semi-join leaf, with no two spellings of one scope during the transition; ADR-0139 D1 (`:128`) refuses that leaf on a write verb.

- **The new leg is a verdict, not a scope — RIGHT.** `assertControlledByParentWrite` (`security-plugin.ts:9066`), when `extractSingleId` (`:7418`) names no row, reads the engine's own dispatch verdict (`resolveEngineUpdateDispatch` / `resolveEngineDeleteDispatch`, `:9125`–`:9146`, the same two predicates the write doors read at `:7346`), and on the dispatch's `multi` verdict collects masters through `controlledByParentPredicateWriteMasters` (`:9429`) and runs `assertControlledByParentChainEditable` (`:9296`) once per distinct master. The method only throws or returns: it writes nothing into `opCtx.ast`, `opCtx.options.where` or the composed `extra` scopes (`:4395`–`:4445`); its read takes `copyOfCallerPredicate`. No master set is composed into the write, so ruling B gets no second spelling.
- **Read scope, objectql and spec untouched — RIGHT.** `computeControlledByParentFilter` (`:8646`) carries no hunk; the file list is three paths, none under `packages/objectql/**` or `packages/spec/**`.
- **Coverage, dispatch verdict by verdict, against what `extractSingleId` reads — RIGHT for the two verbs the card measured.**
  - `by-id` (a truthy scalar id, from the payload or a pure id `where`): `extractSingleId` returns that id, the by-id leg runs as before.
  - `multi` with no scalar `where.id`: the new leg, per master.
  - `multi` with a scalar `where.id` beside other keys (the dispatch's compare-and-set arm): `extractSingleId` returns that id and the by-id leg judges the one row the predicate can reach (the id equality rides the AST, so the written set is at most that row). Judged.
  - `multi` with a falsy scalar id: `extractSingleId` tests type, not truth, so the by-id leg runs on that id — either that row's master is judged or `DetailRecordNotFoundError` (404) refuses. Refused or judged, never unjudged; the envelope quirk predates this card.
  - `reject`: with no single id the gate returns, and the engine refuses the call on the same `executeWithMiddleware` pass before any driver write; with a payload id the by-id leg runs and the engine then refuses. Nothing written either way.
  - `delete` mirrors `update` minus the payload arm (`engine-delete-dispatch.ts:resolveEngineDeleteDispatch`).
  - The lifecycle verbs in step 2.8's list are outside the middleware vocabulary (pinned in `packages/objectql/src/engine-middleware-operation-vocabulary.test.ts`): dormant, unchanged.
  - A nested write (a hook's or cascade's, under the caller's context): the new leg has no `nested` exclusion, so it is judged on the rows the caller can read; the write's AST carries the derived read filter regardless of nesting (`:4412`, under `if (opCtx.ast)` alone), so the rows it writes sit under readable masters. The judged and written sets part only where an authored policy on the detail admits for update what it withholds for select, which a derived object does not author (ADR-0055 §1). The dev disclosed this in the Acceptance notes; residual, not a defect of this diff.
  - Single-row insert: unchanged (`:9121`, the #8688 stand-down at `:9267` holds as before).
  - One further shape in the same gate family, not of the card's measured path, is not shown judged by this diff. Held out of this record under the disclosure ruling; escalated in ③.
- **Envelope — RIGHT.** Every refusal on the new path is built by the gate's own `masterEditDenied` factory passed into the walk: `PermissionDeniedError`, 403, named for the caller's object and operation, leg recorded in `MASTER_EDIT_DENIAL_LEG`. The test compares the live by-id answer (code, status, message) with the other route's answer for the same caller and master, not a literal.
- **Nothing written on refusal — RIGHT.** Step 2.8 (`:3246`, delegator pass `:3256`) runs inside the middleware before `await next()` (`:4498`) and before the readable narrowing (`:4441`); a throw ends the pass before the driver. The test reads every seeded row back unchanged after each refusal.
- **Fail closed where rows cannot be enumerated — RIGHT.** The new leg's `this.ql.find` is not wrapped in `readUnlessRefused` (`:740`), so a declared 4xx on the read propagates as the write's answer (pinned: equal to the read's own refusal); above `PREDICATE_WRITE_READABLE_ID_CAP` (`:772`, `MAX_BULK_PER_ROW_HOOK_ROWS` = 10,000 at `bulk-write-hook-conformance.ts:282`) it throws `predicateWriteReadableCapError` (400 `INVALID_FILTER`, `:775`); a store fault propagates; a stored row with a null master reference throws `MasterReferenceMissingError` (422) as the by-id leg does; a missing engine throws. Contrast kept on purpose: `readableRowsScopeForPredicateWrite` (`:7384`) swallows a refusal as "no narrowing", the gate does not, and the gate runs first.
- **Chain walk extracted verbatim, one copy — RIGHT.** Compared the inline walk at the base `dfe60e3a0c` with `assertControlledByParentChainEditable` at the head: 86 lines each, one comment line differs (the "read above" wording the PR body declares). The file holds exactly one walk header and one `for (;;)`; `assertMasterRowEditable` stays the single copy of the three legs.
- **On-behalf-of — RIGHT.** The gate runs per principal (`:3246`, `:3256`); the row read is under `opCtx.context` on both passes, the walk under each principal's sets and context, as the by-id leg does.
- **No widening of the floor — RIGHT.** `masterGateCoversThisWrite` is set only at step 2.7 (`:3095`) and on a middle hop (`:9625`); the new path sets it nowhere, so the platform ownership floor stays on this shape, as the reworded docblock says.
- **Tests.** The new file drives a real stack (ObjectQL over better-sqlite3, the real plugin, sharing service and middleware); pins 1–5 match the PR body. The ablation table is the dev's claim, read, not re-run.

- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` stands on the PR body and the changeset; the title carries `!`; the changeset is `'@objectstack/plugin-security': minor` with the BREAKING banner — the #24813 shape, which amended 「甲」 rule 2 on #6015 (`6303865025`) prescribes: a narrowing no conversion carries ships now in 18.x as a BREAKING minor. RIGHT.
- What narrows: the accept set of update and delete on a `controlled_by_parent` detail, for a caller the master-edit question refuses — a refusal where a write landed. Nothing widens: no new capability, no composed scope, inserts, by-id writes, system contexts and the read scope unchanged. ADR-0087 category `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is right: no metadata moves, the remedy is a grant.
- Abstract statement — RIGHT under the disclosure ruling: the changeset names no write shape, grant, request or served value; before and now are stated as the master-edit question and the by-id refusal.
- One wording flag, carried to ③: the headline says "every write", the body says inserts are unchanged.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Refuse versus narrow (dev recommends A; seat ruled A in the patch round) — answered, A is right.** Narrowing would compose an editable-master set into the write: a second spelling of a master scope while ruling B retires the id-list for the leaf, and ADR-0139 D1 refuses the leaf on write verbs. Refusing adds no mechanism and is forward-compatible; a later move to narrowing is a widening and reviewable as one.
2. **Comment-only docblock rider at `033fc75a09` — answered, verified.** The commit touches one file, 7 lines in and 3 out, every changed line a comment line, no code token. Sentence one (the `RlsFilterOptions` bullet) is true of the code: the new path sets no vouch and throws rather than scopes, so the floor stays. Sentence two (step 2.7's parenthetical) is true: with no single id, 2.8 judges every master on the `multi` verdict, and on `reject` the write reaches none.

Detail withheld here under the #9387 ruling and returned to the dispatching seat with this record. The seat matches it against the dev's hand-off; if the two differ, it is a second card. For this PR: the headline's "every write" is wider than the body's own "Unchanged: inserts" line; the seat decides whether to narrow the headline to the verbs the card measured before the CHANGELOG line publishes, or to carry the residual on its card. Not introduced by this diff.
4. **Nested writes** — disclosed in the Acceptance notes; judged in ①; residual, not blocking.
